title: Add RAG live-indexer hot-reload quickstart
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a developer-focused quickstart demonstrating an incremental indexer with hot-reload and live dev server. Useful for RAG authoring workflows and debugging streaming index updates.
description:
Background and motivation: Teams building retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows often iterate on doc transforms, index pipelines, and embedding schemas while developing features. This quickstart provides a lightweight local dev runner that watches a content directory, incrementally updates an in-memory index, emits compact trace events, and demonstrates how Redwood's streaming inference routes can use the updated index without restarting services.

Goals: 1) shorten dev feedback loop for RAG authoring, 2) show best-practice index mutations that preserve shard/namespace isolation, 3) provide telemetry probes to validate eventual consistency between index updates and serving behavior.

What this PR changes (high-level commits):
- feat: add live-indexer dev runner and file-watcher (src/live_indexer/*) — core incremental indexer logic, pluggable backends (memory/fs), and simple event API used by the example service.
- feat: add example dev server that integrates indexer + Redwood SDK streaming client (examples/live-indexer-devserver/).
- docs: quickstart guide + troubleshooting (docs/quickstarts/live-indexer-hot-reload.md) with diagrams and recommended sanity checks.
- test: add unit tests for index mutation ordering and a small e2e smoke test that spins up the devserver and simulates file changes (tests/live-indexer-e2e).
- ci: add GitHub Actions job step to run the e2e smoke test on non-main branches (ci/workflows/live-indexer.yml).

Changed files (high level): src/live_indexer/indexer.py, src/live_indexer/watchers.py, src/live_indexer/backends/memory_backend.py, examples/live-indexer-devserver/server.py, examples/live-indexer-devserver/README.md, docs/quickstarts/live-indexer-hot-reload.md, tests/test_indexer_ordering.py, tests/e2e/test_live_indexer_smoke.py, ci/workflows/live-indexer.yml, package.json (dev dependency for fs-watcher), Makefile (dev run target).

Checklist (author): 
- [x] Implementation for in-memory index and file watcher
- [x] Example that demonstrates streaming route re-query without restart
- [x] Quickstart doc with troubleshooting and common pitfalls
- [x] Unit and small e2e test coverage
- [x] CI job to run smoke e2e

Review conversation summary: 
- Diego: "Nice focused quickstart. A couple of nit comments around API names (mutate_index vs apply_patch). Also add a gentle note about ordering guarantees in the docs"
- Author (Maya): "Addressed: renamed apply_patch -> mutate_index to make intent clearer, added explicit ordering guarantees section in docs with example sequence numbers."
- Priya: "Can the devserver simulate delayed embedding computation? We should show a common real-world pattern where emb computation lags the file write."
- Author: "Added optional --simulate-embed-latency flag to the devserver and a short section in troubleshooting showing how the serving route degrades and recovers."
- Liam: "CI was flaky on the first run due to a race in the e2e harness (port reuse). Recommend retry/backoff in the test runner."
- Author: "Fixed: tests/e2e harness now picks ephemeral ports and retries the server startup loop up to 3 times. CI re-run passed."

CI summary: Initial GitHub Actions run failed the e2e smoke test due to port collision (flaky test harness). I pushed a small fix in the e2e harness and re-ran CI; the subsequent run passed all checks (lint, unit, e2e). The PR was merged by squash once reviewers approved.

How to try locally (short): 
1) make dev-run
2) cd examples/live-indexer-devserver && node run-dev (or python -m examples.live_indexer.server)
3) edit examples/live-indexer-devserver/content/*.md and observe index updates in the server logs and the live /debug/last_update endpoint.

Why this is different from other quickstarts: Existing templates focus on orchestration, tool-calling, or large-scale indexing. This quickstart is explicitly developer-centric: minimal infra, fast feedback loop, and concrete probes for index-to-serve consistency useful when authoring retrieval prompts and prompt-driven evals. It is intended for engineers working on RAG feature UX, prompt tuning, or index schema iterations.

Follow-ups and open items:

- Add a demo notebook that shows how to author prompt variants and run quick A/B evaluations against updated index state.

Merge outcome: merged into main on 2026-02-25 via squash. Merge commit message: "Add RAG live-indexer hot-reload quickstart (dev-runner + docs + tests)."
